summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with severe polyarticular joint pain involving both feet, ankles, right knee, and elbow, following a recent switch from colchicine to Uloric for gout management. She reported new paresthesias in her feet and was unable to bear weight. Initial labs showed elevated creatinine at 2.1, consistent with worsening kidney function. Imaging revealed degenerative changes but no acute fractures. Rheumatology consultation suggested possible calcium crystal disease rather than classic gout, given no prior confirmation of uric acid crystals. Treatment included restarting colchicine every other day, reducing Uloric to 80 mg daily, and initiating a six-day prednisone taper for inflammation. Gabapentin was added for neuropathic symptoms. During admission, she developed leukopenia, likely due to colchicine, and a left thumb paronychia, for which she was started on cephalexin. Her pain improved, and she was discharged home with follow-up plans for nephrology and rheumatology. Her kidney function remained stable but elevated, suggesting a possible new baseline.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
